newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo naphtha steady, jet firmer on topper closure.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo naphtha steady, jet firmer on topper closure.

text.p: Naphtha prices were little changed on Friday, but sentiment in the jet kerosene market firmed due to the closure of Japan Energy Corp's Mizushima topper.

Open-specification naphtha for the latter half of February was assessed virtually unchanged from Thursday at $239.00/240.00. It was sold once at $239.50 and again at 239.00 on Thursday. First-half March was quoted at $236.00/237.00, also unchanged from late Thursday. Japan Energy said earlier it was unclear when the refiner would restart its 110,000 barrel-per-day topper at its Mizushima plant, which has been closed since a gas leak accident on Wednesday.
Sanyo Petrochemical's 440,000 tonnes per year ethylene plant at Mizushima procures about 20 percent of its feedstock naphtha from Japan Energy, traders said.
A naphtha trader with Sanyo Petrochemical said the firm had no plans to buy extra spot cargoes at the moment as the shutdown was unlikely to be prolonged.

Japan Energy said it was not planning to import extra jet kerosene cargoes for the time being. However, traders said the closure cast a bullish tone in the jet kerosene market. Levels were notionally assessed at around $2.40 over the mean of Singapore quotes.
